plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like composite flower heads made up of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. The heads track the sun when young. It is widely grown as an ornamental, for seed, and for oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, with major fields in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and France
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west (heliotropism), but mature flowers face east and stop moving.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. It is grown for ornament, perfume, and essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August), with peak bloom in July in many regions
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant blooms on tall stalks. The flowers open in the morning and close at night over several days. It is revered in many Asian cultures.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September), peaking in July and August
plants.location: Asia, including India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and Thailand, and northern Australia; widely cultivated in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt, known as the 'lotus effect', which has inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Chamaenerion angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms spires of vivid magenta-pink flowers, blooming from the bottom of the spike upward. It is among the first plants to colonize burned or disturbed land. It grows in meadows, roadsides, and forest clearings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September)
plants.location: Northern temperate and subarctic regions, including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, Siberia, and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Locals say that when the flowers reach the top of the spike, summer is nearly over, making fireweed a natural seasonal clock.
